draft.headline: Chronic absence is the largest area at 23%, up from 21% in Q1, and it overlaps with academics for 25 students.

keyNumbers.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
students moved to a higher tier

bigPicture.label: chronically absent, up from 21%
bigPicture.point: Largest area, well ahead of academics at 14% and behavior at 7%.
bigPicture.read: Is absence spread across the day or clustered in certain periods? Check period-by-period attendance for flagged students.
bigPicture.do: Pull period-by-period attendance for the 69 flagged students and look for patterns by period within 3 weeks.
bigPicture.doLess: Ease off whole-school attendance reminders aimed at students already attending regularly.

bigPicture.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
bigPicture.point: More than half of the 42 students flagged in academics are also flagged in attendance.
bigPicture.read: Attendance and academics likely travel together here, so one shared plan may fit better than two separate ones.
bigPicture.do: Build one combined attendance-and-grades plan for these students and review it together every 4 weeks.
bigPicture.doLess: Ease off running separate attendance and grades plans for the same students.

bigPicture.label: students moved to a higher tier
bigPicture.point: Fewer than 10 moved to a lower tier, so more students moved up than down.
bigPicture.read: Which flag pushed these students up a tier? Compare Q1 and Q2 attendance lists and course failure lists.
bigPicture.do: Review the 17 students who moved up and assign each one tier 2 support within 2 weeks.

counselor.label: grade 9 chronically absent
counselor.point: Highest of any grade; grade 11 is 14%.
counselor.read: Is this a ninth-grade transition issue or specific periods? Ask students in check-ins and review period attendance.
counselor.do: Start a 6-week attendance check-in group for grade 9 students flagged for attendance.

counselor.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
counselor.point: These students face two flags at once, so a single group can cover both.
counselor.do: Run a 6-week small group combining attendance goals and study skills for students flagged in both areas.
counselor.doLess: Ease off one-time classroom lessons about attendance alone.

administrator.label: chronically absent students in Q2
administrator.do: Have attendance staff run a weekly list of flagged students and near-threshold students for the next 4 weeks.
administrator.doLess: Ease off school-wide attendance incentives that mostly reach students already attending.

administrator.label: students moved to a higher tier
administrator.point: Support has to keep up with students moving up, with fewer than 10 moving down.
administrator.do: Protect weekly MTSS meeting time so the 17 students moving up get plans within 2 weeks.

teachers.label: flagged in academics, up from 12%
teachers.point: Smaller than attendance at 23%, but also growing since Q1.
teachers.read: Are course failures tied to work missed during absences? Compare course failure lists with attendance lists.
teachers.do: Set a 2-week make-up work window after absences in grade 9 courses.
teachers.doLess: Ease off zeros for missed work without a make-up path.

teachers.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
teachers.point: These students are flagged in two areas, so the classroom is a good place to notice change.
teachers.do: Use a first-period check-in routine for these students for 4 weeks, noting attendance and missing work.
teachers.doLess: Ease off public reminders about absences or missing work.

supportTeam.label: newly flagged for attendance since Q1
supportTeam.point: New attendance flags since Q1 mean early contact is still possible.
supportTeam.read: What changed for these students in Q2? Review attendance staff contact logs and period-by-period attendance.
supportTeam.do: Hold a short problem-solving call with each newly flagged student's family within 2 weeks.

supportTeam.label: students moved to a higher tier
supportTeam.point: Compared with fewer than 10 moving down, more students are moving up.
supportTeam.do: Review each of the 17 at the next MTSS meeting, assign one intervention, and recheck at 6 weeks.
supportTeam.doLess: Ease off reviewing every student at the same pace regardless of tier change.

connections.label: flagged in both attendance and academics
connections.point: One shared list lets three roles act on the same students.

steps.step: Share the shared list with teachers and the support team after each check-in cycle.
Send counselors a short weekly note on missing work for students on the list.
Review the shared list at MTSS every 4 weeks and adjust supports.

connections.label: chronically absent students in Q2
connections.point: A weekly list only helps if someone acts on it quickly.

steps.step: Assign staff to run the weekly attendance list and set one shared threshold.
Act on each new name within 2 weeks and record the step taken.

connections.label: grade 9 chronically absent
connections.point: Grade 9 stands highest, so a coordinated start is worth it.

steps.step: Run grade 9 check-ins and share patterns with teachers each 2 weeks.
Flag grade 9 period-level absence patterns to the counselor weekly.
Review the grade 9 schedule for period-level absence clusters this month.

goals.baseline: Q2 share of all students flagged in academics.

goals.baseline: Q2 share of all students in tier 3.

draft.limits: Behavior is not compared with Q1. No areas are missing from the files. Counts under 10 are not shown, and this summary cannot explain why numbers changed or describe individual students.
